newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada reaches deal with provinces on lumber.
newsitem.headline: Canada reaches deal with provinces on lumber.

text.p: Canada said on Tuesday it reached an agreement with its provinces on the allocation of softwood lumber exports to the United States.

An International Trade Department spokesperson said the government reached an agreement with the provinces and the lumber industry on their individual export quotas under an agreement between Ottawa and Washington that was signed in April.
Under the agreement, Canadian lumber exports that exceed quarterly or annual quotas are subject to export fees.

Under the new allocation, which was done on a company by company basis, British Columbia will get 59 percent of the total annual quota for Canada and Quebec will get 23 percent. Ontario will get 10.3 percent and Alberta will be allocated 7.7 percent.

Under the Canada-U.S. agreement shipments of over 14.7 billion board feet a year, or 4.2 billion board feet a quarter will be slapped with an export duty. The quarterly quota for all of Canada is 28.75 percent of the annual limit.
"This plan is balanced and fair to the provinces and to the softwood lumber industry," International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said in a press release.

The new allocation, based on recent export shipment patterns, will go to primary producers and remanufacturers who further process lumber. Wholesalers of lumber will not receive direct allocations, but the government said it had the assurances of primary producers that they will continue to use provincial wholesalers as their distributors to the United States.

"I will monitor the system very closely over the next few months to assure that these assurances are being kept and that the system is working to the benefits of all segments of the lumber industry," Eggleton said.
The allocation will be reviewed annually for the next four years of the life of the Canada-U.S. agreement.

The new plan also allows an allocation of 294 million board feet, or two percent of the annual quota for Canada, to new mills, as well as a 184 million board feet bonus without export fees. The plan would give new mills 150 million board feet with an export fee of US$50 per every 1,000 board feet.
